Looking at this problem, I need to identify the work done by body forces on a fluid element per unit time (power).

## Analysis

**Setting up the physics:**
- For a fluid element, work per unit time = Force · Velocity (dot product)
- The body force per unit mass is **f⃗**
- The element has density ρ and volume dV = dx dy dz

**Determining the total force on the element:**

The mass of the element is:
$$dm = \rho \, dx\,dy\,dz$$

The total body force on the element (force per unit mass × mass):
$$\vec{F}_{body} = \vec{f} \cdot dm = \rho \vec{f} \, dx\,dy\,dz$$

**Computing the work done (power):**

$$d\dot{W} = \vec{F}_{body} \cdot \vec{V} = \rho \vec{f} \cdot \vec{V} \, dx\,dy\,dz$$

## Verification of Units

- ρ: kg/m³
- f⃗: m/s² (force per unit mass)  
- V⃗: m/s
- dx dy dz: m³

Power = (kg/m³)(m/s²)(m/s)(m³) = kg·m²/s³ = W ✓

Option 4 lacks velocity (not work). Option 2 is missing the volume element. Option 1 would only be correct if f⃗ were already force per unit volume, but the standard convention is that f⃗ represents force per unit mass.
